title: Dressing changes for a diabetic foot wound
what: A nurse or doctor cleans the wound on your foot, removes dead tissue, and puts on a dressing. This is repeated regularly until the wound heals.
why: For ulcers and wounds on the foot in people with diabetes.
duration: a dressing change usually takes 15 to 40 minutes; treatment lasts weeks to months
tell_doctor: A fever, or swelling or redness of the foot
Whether your leg hurts when walking

prepare.title: Off-loading
prepare.text: Do not put weight on the wound. Use the off-loading shoe or dressing your doctor prescribed.

prepare.title: Sugar
prepare.text: Keep your sugar in the target range, since healing depends on it.

prepare.title: Shoes
prepare.text: Soft shoes without seams, with room for the dressing.

bring: A glucose meter or sugar records
steps: The wound is rinsed and examined
The wound is treated and a new dressing is put on
The doctor assesses how healing is going
You are told when the next dressing change is
feel: With diabetes you often feel little pain, which does not mean the wound is harmless
Cleaning the wound can sometimes be unpleasant
after: Keep the dressing dry and do not take it off yourself
Check both feet every day, using a mirror
Come for dressing changes on schedule
red_flags: Redness that spreads, swelling, or a bad smell
The foot became cold, pale, or black: see a doctor urgently
Sugar is very high and does not come down

faq.q: Why does the wound take so long to heal?
faq.a: With diabetes, blood supply and protection from infection are weaker. Off-loading, sugar control, and regular dressing changes help.

faq.q: Can I treat the wound at home with ointments?
faq.a: Do not use any products without your doctor's order. Wrong care can make the wound worse.

reminders.text: Foot dressing change tomorrow. Bring your sugar records and off-loading shoe.
